summary: Takao Maruyama studied Buddhist studies at Tohoku University (~1957–1962). He held posts at Rissho University (assistant professor attested 1972, professor attested 1981), Shinshu University (professor attested 1983–1984, professor emeritus attested 2001), and Mejiro University (professor attested 1988).

A scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and history, Moriyasu studied at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1976) and Osaka University (~1991–1992). He held posts at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, Kanazawa University, and Osaka University (professor ~1992–2013).

Takao Yamagata worked in religious studies, completing his studies at Tohoku University (~1952–1961). He held a post at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (~1970–2002) and served as president of the Association for the Study of Indian Religions (attested 1997).
Takashi Hidaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He served as an open-call researcher at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and as a part-time lecturer at Otani University (attested 2014).

Iwata specialized in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, studying at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg under Akira Hirakawa, Albrecht Wezler, and Lambert Schmithausen. He taught at Waseda University as an assistant professor (~1988–1993) and professor (~1993–2015).
Takashi Maeda studied Buddhist studies and Indology in the doctoral program at Tohoku University. His career includes serving as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995 and 2006).
Takashi Nakao studied Buddhist studies and history/archaeology at Rissho University (~1950–1957). He later served as an emeritus professor at Rissho University (~2002–2020).

A specialist in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Takashi Ogawa studied at Komazawa University (~1980–1986) and Peking University (~1986–1988). He became an assistant professor at Komazawa University around 1991.
Specializing in Sinology and religious studies, Takashi Yamada studied at Hosei University (~1974–1983). He later served as an assistant professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto (~1994).
Takatoshi Ito worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held a position as professor at Komazawa University (attested 1978–1981 and 1991).
Takatoshi Nakamura worked in Buddhist studies, studying under Ryukai Mano in 1979. He held a position as an assistant at Taisho University (attested 1978).

Hayashi worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Delhi (attested 1996). He held posts at Tohoku University (attested 1997), Sendai College (associate professor attested 2008), and Hosen Gakuen College (professor attested 2015).

Takayasu Kimura specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies, completing doctoral studies at Taisho University. He held positions as a researcher at the Buzan-ha Institute of Modern Mission (attested 1995) and lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995).
Takayasu Suzuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–1996). He became a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University around 2008.
Takayoshi Namikawa specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University (~1966–1974) and later served there as a professor (~1991–2018).

Takayuki Hirosawa studied Buddhist studies and Indology at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. His posts include being a group member (until 1991) and later professor (attested 2014) at Taisho University.
Takeo Hibino studied Sinology and history at Kyoto University (~1935–1938). He later held posts at Otemon Gakuin University (~1979–1984) and Otemae University (~1984–1988).

Takeshi Fujii specialized in Indology and history, studying at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1974–1981). He held a post at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1993–2021) and taught Kei Kataoka.

Takeshi Umehara studied philosophy and Japanology at Kyoto University (~1945–1948) and Nagoya University. He held posts at Ryukoku University, Ritsumeikan University (professor ~1967–1972), the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (director general ~1987–1995), and the Institute of Technologists.

Takudo Ishikawa worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts as a researcher at the Jodo Shu Research Institute (attested 2005) and as a specially appointed full-time lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2015).
